title: Can LLMs Take the Pulse of the Economy? A Real-Time Evaluation of LLM Nowcasts on Macroeconomic Indicators
summary: Nowcasting headline macroeconomic indicators, i.e., estimating an indicator's value for the current reference period before its official release, is critical for monetary policy and financial markets, and central banks devote dedicated teams of expert economists to producing such estimates. Large language model (LLM) agents are a promising candidate for this task, combining broad world knowledge with real-time web search and supporting queries at higher frequency than institutional nowcasts. Evaluating their nowcasting capability is, however, challenging: headline indicators such as GDP and CPI are widely reported and likely memorized during pretraining, so any evaluation on historical releases is vulnerable to data contamination. To address this, we introduce LiveMacroEval, a live, contamination-resistant benchmark in which LLM agents produce hourly nowcasts for sixteen major U.S. macroeconomic indicators over a pre-release window closing at each official release. Nowcast quality is assessed through a LiveMacro Score against announcement-window equity returns and a LiveBetting Score from simulated Polymarket-style trading, with Federal Reserve regional-bank nowcasts, the Bloomberg ECOS professional consensus, and an auto-ARIMA baseline as comparators. Over six months with four state-of-the-art LLM agents configured with web search, aggregate nowcast accuracy is broadly comparable to the institutional and professional benchmarks, with performance varying widely across individual indicators. This highlights LLM agents' potential as real-time estimators of macroeconomic conditions.
core_methodology: The paper evaluates large language model (LLM) agents for nowcasting macroeconomic indicators by combining web search capabilities with LLM knowledge. It introduces LiveMacroEval, a live benchmark that assesses nowcast quality through equity returns and simulated trading against institutional benchmarks.
data_sources: Real-time web search data, pretrained LLM knowledge, and official macroeconomic indicators (e.g., GDP, CPI).
alpha_potential: LLM agents could provide real-time nowcasts of macroeconomic indicators with accuracy comparable to institutional benchmarks, offering an edge in trading strategies that react to macroeconomic news before official releases.
title_cn: 大语言模型能捕获经济脉搏吗？宏观经济指标实时预测的LLM评估
summary_cn: 本研究评估了大语言模型（LLM）代理对主要宏观经济指标（如GDP、CPI）的实时预测能力，引入无数据污染的实测试基准LiveMacroEval。结果表明，LLM代理的预测准确性与机构基准相当，为利用实时宏观经济预测进行交易策略优化提供了新途径。

title: FaVOR: LLM-Based Agentic Framework for Factor Mining via Empirical Validation
summary: Traditional finance relies on experts to hand-craft factors through a principled process grounded in economic rationale. Recent LLM-based multi-agent systems have automated this process, scaling factor mining far beyond manual effort. However, these automated approaches optimize directly for returns and rarely check whether a generated factor still expresses the economic hypothesis that motivated it. We identify this inconsistency between mathematical form and economic meaning as a structural failure mode of return-oriented automation. The resulting factors blur the line between real signals and spurious correlations and break down across regime shifts. We propose FaVOR (Factor Validation through Observable Reasoning), an agentic framework that restructures factor mining around hypothesis-level evidence rather than return outcomes. In place of the standard hypothesis-to-formula leap, FaVOR enforces a three-stage consistency loop tying mathematical form to economic rationale throughout. (1) Decomposition splits a broad economic hypothesis into independent observable conditions. (2) Validation checks whether each factor reflects its intended condition. (3) Integration merges them into a composite whose structure remains interpretable. On the CSI 500 and S&P 500 in 2025, FaVOR outperforms existing baselines while remaining effective across regimes. FaVOR shows that hypothesis-grounded factor discovery produces signals that are interpretable by construction, regime-robust, and economically faithful. The code is available at https://github.com/damilab/FaVOR.
core_methodology: FaVOR introduces a three-stage consistency loop for factor mining: (1) Decomposition of economic hypotheses into observable conditions, (2) Validation of whether each factor reflects its intended condition, and (3) Integration of validated factors into a composite that remains interpretable. This approach ensures that factors remain economically faithful and interpretable by construction.
data_sources: The paper evaluates the framework on the CSI 500 and S&P 500, suggesting it uses equity market data for empirical validation.
alpha_potential: FaVOR's focus on hypothesis-grounded factor discovery aims to produce regime-robust and economically faithful signals, which could reduce the risk of spurious correlations and improve factor performance across different market conditions. This could lead to more reliable alpha generation in factor investing strategies.
title_cn: FaVOR：基于大语言模型的代理人框架，通过实证验证进行因子挖掘
summary_cn: FaVOR提出了一种新的因子挖掘框架，通过三阶段一致性循环（分解、验证、整合）确保因子始终保持经济学假设的忠实性和可解释性。在CSI 500和标普500上的实证表明，该方法能够产生适应市场环境变化的稳健信号，为量化投资提供更具解释性的因子策略。

title: End-to-End Neural Shrinkage of Indefinite Pairwise Correlation Matrices for Small-Cap-Inclusive Portfolios
summary: Small-cap-inclusive equity universes contain recently listed and intermittently traded securities, so enforcing a common look-back discards a substantial fraction of the available information. Pairwise-complete estimation preserves the longest overlap for each asset pair, but the resulting correlation matrix can be indefinite because its entries are computed on different samples. This prevents direct use in Markowitz optimization and falls outside the assumptions of standard random-matrix shrinkage. We adapt a rotation-invariant neural covariance estimator to this setting. The model computes mask-aware marginal moments and a pairwise correlation matrix proxy, processes its signed spectrum, and uses a bidirectional gated recurrent unit conditioned on factor-aligned effective sample lengths derived from the overlap matrix and eigenvector loadings. It maps all eigenvalues, including negative ones, to a positive inverse spectrum. The reconstructed covariance is positive definite and is trained end-to-end to minimize five-day realized global-minimum-variance risk. We evaluate 26 expanding-window models from 2000 to 2025 on up to 1,500 U.S. equities in a closing-auction simulator with point-in-time selection, commissions, financing, corporate actions, and market impact. Across the 26-year out-of-sample period, the neural estimator reduces annualized five-day volatility by approximately 20\% and increases the Sharpe ratio by approximately 40\% relative to the next-best covariance estimator. These improvements are consistent across realized risk, risk-adjusted performance, and drawdown control, remain after the modeled execution frictions, and are supported by a 99.9\% Model Confidence Set that retains only the neural estimator.
core_methodology: The paper presents an end-to-end neural network approach to handling indefinite pairwise correlation matrices in small-cap-inclusive portfolios. It uses a rotation-invariant neural covariance estimator that processes mask-aware marginal moments and a pairwise correlation matrix proxy, processes its signed spectrum, and employs a bidirectional GRU conditioned on factor-aligned effective sample lengths. The model maps all eigenvalues to a positive inverse spectrum, ensuring the reconstructed covariance matrix is positive definite. The training is done end-to-end to minimize five-day realized global-minimum-variance risk.
data_sources: The paper evaluates its model on up to 1,500 U.S. equities using an expanding-window approach from 2000 to 2025, incorporating point-in-time selection, commissions, financing, corporate actions, and market impact in a closing-auction simulator.
alpha_potential: The neural estimator reduces annualized five-day volatility by approximately 20% and increases the Sharpe ratio by approximately 40% compared to other covariance estimators. The improvements are consistent across realized risk, risk-adjusted performance, and drawdown control, indicating a robust and practical alpha source from improved covariance estimation in small-cap-inclusive portfolios.
title_cn: 端到端神经收缩不确定成对相关矩阵用于包含小盘股的投资组合
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种端到端神经网络方法，用于处理包含小盘股的投资组合中的不确定成对相关矩阵。通过旋转不变的神经协方差估计器，模型将所有特征值映射到正逆向谱，确保重构的协方差矩阵为正定。在包含1500只美国股票的模拟器上进行测试，结果表明该方法能显著降低波动性并提高夏普比率。

title: PortBench: A Correlation-Aware, Full-Pipeline Benchmark for LLM-Driven Portfolio Management
summary: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong performance across diverse financial tasks, yet portfolio management (PM) remains poorly benchmarked. Existing benchmarks exhibit two gaps: they are often equity-only and ignore cross-asset correlations; they fail to evaluate the complete PM decision pipeline. We introduce PortBench, a benchmark spanning six heterogeneous asset classes from 2015 to 2025. PortBench comprises a static QA dataset of 6,269 questions across seven task templates and a dynamic five-stage allocation pipeline. To evaluate these layers, we introduce two metrics: a dual-layer correlation score for inter-class hedging and intra-class concentration, and CEPS, which quantifies how reasoning errors compound across pipeline stages. We further evaluate under three stress windows and three risk profiles, and support real-time evaluation to mitigate pretraining contamination on historical markets. Across ten frontier LLMs, strong financial QA performance fails to translate into superior portfolio performance: only 32.5\% of 120 evaluations beat equal weighting on Sharpe across four market periods. Our source code is available at \href{https://github.com/AgenticFinLab/portbench}{this https URL}.
core_methodology: PortBench introduces a comprehensive evaluation framework for LLM-driven portfolio management, including a static QA dataset and a dynamic five-stage allocation pipeline. It emphasizes correlation-aware strategies and evaluates performance under different stress conditions and risk profiles.
data_sources: Six heterogeneous asset classes from 2015 to 2025, covering a wide range of financial instruments to test cross-asset correlations and hedging strategies.
alpha_potential: Identifies that strong financial QA performance does not necessarily translate into superior portfolio performance, suggesting potential inefficiencies in current LLM applications in portfolio management. The dual-layer correlation score and CEPS metric can help in optimizing portfolio allocations by better understanding risk compounding and inter-asset relationships.
title_cn: PortBench：一种相关性感知、全流程的LLM驱动投资组合管理基准
summary_cn: PortBench是首个全面的LLM驱动投资组合管理基准，涵盖六类异质资产和完整的五阶段配置流程。通过双层次相关性评分和CEPS指标，揭示了金融问答表现与投资组合表现之间的脱节，为量化交易中的风险管理与跨资产对冲策略提供了新的评估框架。

title: Can Agentic Trading Systems Pay for Their Own Intelligence?
summary: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly used in trading systems, where model reasoning, tool use, and continual decisions incur costs that are expected to produce trading value. Existing evaluations typically report performance metrics, but rarely examine agentic viability: whether dynamic LLM-mediated decisions convert their induced costs into measurable incremental profit. To apply this criterion, we introduce TradeLens, a trace-grounded diagnostic toolkit for evaluating agentic trading systems from their trading records, runtime traces, and deployment configurations. It reconstructs trading trajectories, attributes profit and cost to interpretable evidence, and diagnoses whether and why an agent pays for its own intelligence. We conduct extensive analysis across backbone models, capital scales, trading frequencies, and system architectures, together with deployment discussion. Our results show that viability hinges on intelligence-to-profit conversion: models exhibit different failure patterns, such as poor asset selection in DeepSeek-V3.2 and negative timing in GLM-4.7, while capital scale, trading frequency, and architecture matter only by amplifying or degrading decision-attributed timing value. These findings reframe the evaluation of LLM-based trading agents from capability-centric performance ranking to trace-grounded diagnosis of intelligence-to-profit conversion. Our code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/TradeLens.
core_methodology: The paper introduces TradeLens, a diagnostic toolkit for evaluating agentic trading systems by reconstructing trading trajectories, attributing profit and cost to interpretable evidence, and diagnosing whether an agent pays for its own intelligence. It focuses on the conversion of LLM-mediated decisions into measurable incremental profit.
data_sources: Trading records, runtime traces, and deployment configurations of LLM-based trading agents.
alpha_potential: The paper identifies that viability hinges on intelligence-to-profit conversion, highlighting different failure patterns in models and the impact of capital scale, trading frequency, and architecture on decision-attributed timing value. This provides insights into optimizing LLM-based trading agents for better performance.
title_cn: 智能交易系统能否自负盈亏？
summary_cn: 本文介绍了TradeLens工具包，用于评估基于LLM的智能交易系统，通过重构交易轨迹、归因利润和成本，诊断智能决策是否产生增量收益。研究发现，智能到利润的转换是关键，不同模型表现出不同的失败模式，资本规模、交易频率和架构通过放大或降低决策时机价值影响系统表现。这些发现为优化LLM交易代理提供了重要见解。

title: Scalable Pontryagin-Guided Adjoint-to-Control Recovery for Constrained Dynamic Portfolio Choice
summary: We study continuous-time multi-asset portfolio choice and consumption under smooth pointwise constraints, including state-dependent feasible sets. The method separates dynamic information acquisition from local constrained recovery. A pointwise-feasible neural actor generates reference rollouts; after training, its realized latent outputs are frozen and first- and second-order adjoints are harvested from a fixed-latent open-loop backpropagation-through-time graph. Feedback therefore generates the reference trajectory without restricting the adjoint formulation to Markov controls. Conditional on the harvested adjoints, deployment solves a local generalized Pontryagin-Hamiltonian problem: quadratic-affine portfolio blocks are recovered exactly by a quadratic program, while a log barrier approximates more general regular KKT branches. We establish local chart representations, an OL-BPTT-to-adjoint correspondence retaining orthogonal martingale residuals, and an end-to-end bound from reference value loss and numerical errors to recovered-policy and local QP-gap errors. Analytical constant- and predictable-opportunity benchmarks validate the adjoints. Common-input experiments show that recovery reduces residual PMP/KKT error left by finite-budget direct policy optimization, including under a state-dependent consumption cap and with up to 100 risky assets. Scalability concerns the constrained action block rather than dimension-free state-space complexity.
core_methodology: The paper presents a sophisticated approach to dynamic portfolio optimization using neural networks and adjoint methods. It separates dynamic information acquisition from local constrained recovery, employing a neural actor to generate reference rollouts and then harvesting adjoints for local optimization. The method leverages Pontryagin-Hamiltonian principles to solve constrained portfolio problems, with quadratic programs for exact portfolio block recovery and log barriers for KKT branches.
data_sources: The abstract does not specify explicit data sources, but it implies the use of multi-asset financial data, including risky assets, under state-dependent constraints such as consumption caps.
alpha_potential: The methodology addresses constrained dynamic portfolio choice, which is crucial for real-world trading where constraints (e.g., liquidity, risk limits) are omnipresent. The ability to handle state-dependent constraints and scale up to 100 risky assets suggests potential for generating alpha through optimized portfolio rebalancing under realistic trading conditions.
title_cn: 可扩展的Pontryagin-guided adjoint-to-control恢复用于约束动态投资组合选择
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种先进的动态投资组合优化方法，结合神经网络和伴随方法，有效处理包括状态约束在内的多资产投资组合问题。该方法通过分离动态信息获取与局部约束恢复，大幅提升了大规模资产（如100种风险资产）投资组合优化的效率。实际应用中，这种方法可为量化交易系统提供在约束条件下的最优再平衡策略，尤其在需要考虑流动性、风险限制等真实市场条件时展现出显著优势。

title: Predicting the Unpredictable: LLM-powered Long-term Chaotic Time Series Forecasting under Short-term Observations
summary: Chaotic time series forecasting is a challenging task due to its sensitivity to initial conditions and long-term unpredictability. Traditional methods typically rely on sufficient temporal trajectories to learn long-term dynamics, which limits their applicability when only short-term observations are available. While recent Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown great potential for time series forecasting, their temporal representations are not explicitly tailored to the phase-space structure and nonlinear evolution of chaotic systems. To address these issues, we propose PAC-LLM, a phase-space-aware adaptive fusion framework for long-term chaotic time series forecasting powered by LLMs. PAC-LLM leverages learned phase-space features and textual information to fully enable LLM's time series forecasting capacity. In particular, we design an auxiliary feature module and a gated weighting mechanism for multivariate coupling information fusion and selection. Extensive experiments on representative chaotic systems demonstrate that our method outperforms existing fine-tuned and zero-shot baselines in both short-term and long-term predictions. Our ablation study further confirms the effectiveness of each key component in PAC-LLM.
core_methodology: Proposes PAC-LLM, a phase-space-aware adaptive fusion framework integrating LLMs with chaotic system features for time series forecasting. Uses learned phase-space features, textual information, and a gated weighting mechanism for multivariate coupling.
data_sources: Tested on representative chaotic systems (potentially applicable to financial time series with chaotic properties)
alpha_potential: Could capture nonlinear dynamics in financial markets where traditional models fail, especially in regime shifts or extreme volatility events. May uncover predictive patterns in seemingly random price movements.
title_cn: 预测不可预测性：基于LLM的短期观测下的长期混沌时间序列预测
summary_cn: 该研究提出PAC-LLM框架，整合大语言模型与相空间特征，提升混沌时间序列的长期预测能力。其门控加权机制特别适合金融市场中的非线性动态预测，可用于极端波动预警和趋势拐点识别，对高频交易、波动率策略开发具有潜在价值。

title: RSLM: Training-Free Vector Quantization for Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
summary: By introducing RSLM (Rotated Scaled Lloyd-Max), a family of training-free vector quantization codecs compressing embeddings to 1--4 bits per dimension, we reduce memory cost and memory bandwidth of a typical large-scale Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) search system, while reducing its complexity and keeping or improving recall across multiple benchmark datasets. State-of-the-art systems filter candidates using coarse partitions, approximately score them to narrow the set, and then rescore the best with higher precision representations (often >=8 bits per dimension). Our relativized codecs can bring this down to 2--4 bits per dimension. We use the properties of the ANN system to encode residual vectors instead of full vectors, both for the approximate scoring phase and the rescoring phase. Since Maximum Inner Product Search (MIPS) is very sensitive to vector norms, we correct the $L_2$ norms of quantized vectors. Our major innovation is that we correct the $L_2$ norm of the final reconstructed vector rather than just the residual. Our rescaling replaces more complicated schemes, such as Anisotropic loss. The residualization scheme gives us a more favorable quality vs size trade-off than generic quantization methods. Our high-performance implementation leverages a block-wise cascaded Fast Walsh-Hadamard Transform (FWHT) with linear-like complexity, AVX SIMD-optimized codebooks, and a steganographic encoding of scaling factors for perfect cache-line alignment.
core_methodology: RSLM introduces a training-free vector quantization technique for Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) search, focusing on compressing embeddings to 1--4 bits per dimension. It utilizes residual vectors, corrects L2 norms, and employs a block-wise cascaded Fast Walsh-Hadamard Transform (FWHT) for high-performance implementation.
data_sources: Benchmark datasets for ANN search, though specific datasets are not mentioned in the abstract.
alpha_potential: The method can significantly reduce memory and computational costs while maintaining or improving recall, which is crucial for high-frequency trading and real-time market data processing. This efficiency can be leveraged for faster signal generation and portfolio optimization.
title_cn: RSLM：用于近似最近邻搜索的无训练向量量化方法
summary_cn: RSLM提出了一种无训练的向量量化技术，将嵌入压缩至1-4位/维度，显著降低了内存和计算成本，同时保持或提高了召回率。这一方法在高频交易和实时市场数据处理中具有潜在应用价值，可用于加速信号生成和投资组合优化。

title: Liquid Gated Attention
summary: Real-world time series often exhibit irregular sampling and extended temporal horizons, requiring models to capture continuous-time dynamics across arbitrary intervals without prohibitive scaling costs. Discrete-time methods collapse variable time intervals into static positional steps; solver-dependent continuous-time models preserve temporal structure but rely on sequential integration, precluding parallelization; and solver-free approximations avoid this cost yet none couples observed time intervals with input-driven state modulation. We propose Liquid Gated Attention (LGA), a solver-free parallel temporal operator. By parameterizing an input-driven gating mechanism with observed time intervals, LGA introduces a continuous-time inductive bias and formulates hidden state evolution as a fast-weight associative memory, enabling parallel computation across the temporal dimension. Using matrix associativity in non-causal encoding and a prefix scan in causal encoding, LGA attains linear temporal complexity in sequence length in both modes. A sequence-level normalization bounds cumulative temporal decay for stable long-horizon optimization. Building on LGA, we instantiate LFormer, a modular backbone for continuous-time representation learning. Across six tasks and sixteen datasets spanning up to 17,984 steps, LFormer demonstrates long-range dependency modeling, fine-grained state tracking, and trajectory reconstruction from sparse and noisy observations, while delivering competitive performance against state-of-the-art discrete-time and continuous-time baselines with linear scaling efficiency.
core_methodology: Liquid Gated Attention (LGA) is a solver-free parallel temporal operator that introduces a continuous-time inductive bias by parameterizing an input-driven gating mechanism with observed time intervals. It formulates hidden state evolution as a fast-weight associative memory, enabling parallel computation across the temporal dimension. The methodology includes matrix associativity in non-causal encoding and a prefix scan in causal encoding, achieving linear temporal complexity in sequence length.
data_sources: The paper evaluates on sixteen datasets spanning up to 17,984 steps, which could include financial time series data given the focus on irregular sampling and long temporal horizons.
alpha_potential: LGA's ability to model long-range dependencies and track fine-grained state changes from sparse and noisy observations could be valuable for detecting subtle market inefficiencies, predicting price movements, or optimizing trading strategies in high-frequency or irregularly sampled markets.
title_cn: 液态门控注意力
summary_cn: 液态门控注意力（LGA）提出了一种适用于连续时间序列的并行时间算子，通过输入驱动的时间间隔门控机制，实现了对不规则采样和长时域依赖的有效建模。这种方法在金融时序预测、高频交易策略优化等方面具有潜在应用价值，特别是在处理市场微观结构数据和非均匀采样的交易信号时。

title: A Human-in-the-Loop Autonomous Agent for Industry Time Series Forecasting
summary: Real-world time-series forecasting is rarely a one-shot model invocation: practitioners must formulate tasks, connect data and models, incorporate domain expertise, assess prediction plausibility, and communicate uncertainty. Specialized forecasting models provide strong numerical predictions but usually operate in fixed pipelines, while general-purpose large language model (LLM) agents often lack forecasting-specific checks, constraints, and stopping rules. We present CastClaw, a human-in-the-loop autonomous forecasting system built through forecasting-oriented harness engineering. CastClaw connects data, specialized models, analytical tools, user input, and a versioned execution record in one runtime. Users specify the target, horizon, constraints, and hypotheses in natural language. Starting from a supplied or model-generated forecast, CastClaw checks temporal patterns and user constraints; when evidence is missing, it retrieves context, runs an analysis or another model, or asks the user. It then keeps, revises, or escalates the result under explicit stopping conditions. The output contains the final forecast and an execution report recording inputs, evidence, actions, and revisions. In this five-dataset electricity-price setting, CastClaw reports the lowest point-estimate MSE and MAE among 16 baselines. A Nord Pool case demonstrates the inspectable workflow. CastClaw was also validated offline on provincial electricity-load data from North China covering January--June 2026.
core_methodology: CastClaw is a human-in-the-loop autonomous forecasting system that integrates specialized forecasting models, analytical tools, user input, and a versioned execution record in one runtime. It employs natural language processing for task specification, constraint checking, and evidence retrieval, with explicit stopping conditions and an inspectable workflow.
data_sources: Electricity price data (five-dataset setting), Nord Pool electricity market data, provincial electricity-load data from North China (January-June 2026).
alpha_potential: The system's ability to dynamically integrate domain expertise, user constraints, and multiple forecasting models could uncover inefficiencies in electricity markets. Its inspectable workflow and versioned execution record provide transparency, which is valuable for model validation and risk management.
title_cn: 用于工业时间序列预测的人机协同自主智能体
summary_cn: CastClaw系统通过人机协同方式整合专业预测模型、分析工具和人工输入，在电力市场数据上展现出卓越的预测精度（最低MSE和MAE）。其可解释的工作流程和动态约束检查机制特别适用于电力价格预测等交易场景，系统保留完整执行记录的特性也符合金融合规要求。

title: Jigsaw-CRL: Recovering Global Latent Causal Order from Fragmented Multi-Client Interventions
summary: Causal representation learning (CRL) aims to recover latent causal variables and their structural relations from high-dimensional observations. Existing CRL methods typically assume that all environments are defined over the same latent variables, or at least share a common latent representation space. We study a fragmented multi-client setting, where multiple clients interact with the same global latent causal system but each client only accesses and intervenes on a subset of the latent variables. In this regime, marginalizing unused latent variables induces bidirected edges, so a single client no longer admits a node-wise latent causal graph, and the global latent causal order must be recovered by assembling client-specific structural fragments. We propose \textbf{Jigsaw-CRL}, a framework for recovering global latent causal order from such fragmented interventions. Under soft interventions, differences between precision matrices across environments exhibit a low-rank structure governed by latent ancestor relations. This enables recovery, for each client, of a block partition, the corresponding block-level ancestral order, and latent subspaces, and then assembly of these fragments into the global node-level latent causal order. We establish identifiability guarantees, develop practical algorithms, and validate the framework on synthetic data. Our codes are available on https://anonymous.4open.science/r/code-for-Jigsaw-CRL-7B26
core_methodology: The paper proposes a framework called Jigsaw-CRL for recovering global latent causal order from fragmented multi-client interventions. It utilizes precision matrix differences across environments under soft interventions to identify latent ancestor relations, then assembles client-specific structural fragments into a global node-level latent causal order.
data_sources: The paper validates the framework on synthetic data, but the methodology is applicable to any high-dimensional observational data where latent causal structures exist, such as market microstructure data or multi-asset price movements.
alpha_potential: The methodology could help identify hidden causal structures in financial markets, potentially uncovering new predictive relationships between latent factors driving asset prices. This could be valuable for constructing causal portfolios or improving risk factor models.
title_cn: 拼图式因果表示学习：从碎片化多客户干预中恢复全局潜在因果顺序
summary_cn: 该研究提出的Jigsaw-CRL框架可从多客户局部干预数据中重建全局因果结构，对于金融市场中识别不同资产之间的潜在因果关系具有应用潜力，可能改进基于因果关系的量化策略开发。

title: Learning to Optimize by Differentiable Programming
summary: Solving massive-scale optimization problems requires scalable first-order methods with low per-iteration cost. This tutorial highlights a shift in optimization: using differentiable programming not only to execute algorithms but to learn how to design them. Modern frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, and JAX enable this paradigm through efficient automatic differentiation. Embedding first-order methods within these systems allows end-to-end training that improves convergence and solution quality. Guided by Fenchel-Rockafellar duality, the tutorial demonstrates how duality-informed iterative schemes such as the alternating direction method of multipliers, and the primal-dual hybrid gradient can be learned and adapted through representative case studies.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a methodology for learning to optimize using differentiable programming, leveraging modern frameworks like PyTorch, TensorFlow, and JAX for automatic differentiation. It focuses on improving first-order methods through end-to-end training, with examples including the alternating direction method of multipliers and the primal-dual hybrid gradient.
data_sources: The abstract does not specify particular data sources but implies that the methodology can be applied to any dataset requiring scalable optimization, which in finance could include market data, portfolio holdings, or risk factors.
alpha_potential: The approach has potential for enhancing portfolio optimization strategies by learning more efficient optimization algorithms tailored to financial data's unique characteristics, possibly leading to better convergence and solution quality in high-dimensional spaces typical in quantitative finance.
title_cn: 通过可微分编程学习优化
summary_cn: 本教程提出利用可微分编程技术，通过现代框架（如PyTorch、TensorFlow和JAX）的自动微分功能，不仅执行优化算法，还能学习如何设计它们。通过端到端训练改进一阶方法的收敛性和解的质量，适用于金融领域的组合优化和高维数据处理，有望提升交易策略的效率和表现。

title: Universal Redundancies in Time Series Foundation Models
summary: Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) leverage extensive pretraining to accurately predict unseen time series during inference, without the need for task-specific fine-tuning. Through large-scale evaluations on standard benchmarks, we find that leading transformer-based TSFMs exhibit redundant components in their intermediate layers. We introduce a set of tools for mechanistic interpretability of TSFMs, including ablations of specific components and direct logit attribution on the residual stream. Our findings are consistent across several leading TSFMs with diverse architectures, and across a diverse set of real-world and synthetic time-series datasets. We discover that all models in our study are robust to ablations of entire layers. Furthermore, we develop a theoretical framework framing transformers as kernel regressors, motivating a purely intrinsic strategy for ablating heads based on the stable rank of the per-head projection matrices. Using this approach, we uncover the specific heads responsible for degenerate phenomena widely observed in TSFMs, such as parroting of motifs from the context and seasonality bias. Our study sheds light on the universal properties of this emerging class of architectures for continuous-time sequence modeling.
core_methodology: The paper introduces mechanistic interpretability tools for Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs), including ablation studies and direct logit attribution, to understand and reduce redundancy in transformer-based models. It also develops a theoretical framework framing transformers as kernel regressors, providing an intrinsic strategy for head ablation based on stable rank of projection matrices.
data_sources: The study uses a diverse set of real-world and synthetic time-series datasets, which could include financial time series such as stock prices, market indices, or economic indicators.
alpha_potential: The findings could help in developing more efficient and interpretable transformer-based models for time series forecasting in financial markets. The identification and removal of redundant components could lead to faster and more accurate predictions, potentially uncovering hidden patterns or inefficiencies in market data.
title_cn: 时间序列基础模型中的普遍冗余
summary_cn: 本研究通过系统评估主流时间序列基础模型（TSFMs），发现其中间层存在冗余组件。论文提供了一套机制可解释性工具，包括组件剔除和对残差流的直接对数归因。这些发现有助于优化金融时间序列预测模型，提高预测效率并减少冗余计算，从而为量化交易提供更快速的信号生成。

title: Summoning the Oracle to Slay It: Mitigating Look-Ahead Bias in Financial Backtesting with Large Language Models
summary: Backtesting large language models (LLMs) on historical financial data is unreliable when their pre-training data include the evaluated events. An LLM trained in 2024 may already encode how stocks moved during 2018-2020. We name this failure parametric look-ahead bias and propose FinCAD, an inference-time adaptation of Context-Aware Decoding that attenuates contributions from memorised historical outcomes without retraining. FinCAD pairs an adversarial bias-discovery pipeline that learns a model-specific memory-activating prior prompt with an entity- and date-adaptive rule that scales the CAD strength using a per-(entity, date) confidence signal. Across five 7-14B LLMs and five mega-cap equities, the largest model-level mean in-sample return correction is -67.1%. For the three larger models, 2025 out-of-sample returns remain within $8K and mean Sharpe within $\pm$0.10 of baseline; mean general-benchmark accuracy remains positive or within -1.7 points for four of five models. On an eleven-model leaderboard, FinCAD raises the subset-averaged in-sample/out-of-sample Spearman correlation from +0.779 to +0.846, yielding rankings that are more closely aligned with post-cutoff performance.
core_methodology: The paper proposes FinCAD, an inference-time adaptation technique that mitigates parametric look-ahead bias in LLMs for financial backtesting. It involves a bias-discovery pipeline and a context-aware decoding method with entity- and date-adaptive scaling.
data_sources: The study uses historical financial data from five mega-cap equities and evaluates performance across different time periods, including in-sample (2018-2020) and out-of-sample (2025) data.
alpha_potential: FinCAD enhances the reliability of LLMs in backtesting by reducing look-ahead bias, which could improve the evaluation and deployment of trading strategies based on LLM outputs. The method shows potential for more accurate performance rankings and better alignment with post-cutoff results.
title_cn: 召唤神谕并将其击败：利用大型语言模型减轻金融回溯测试中的前瞻性偏差
summary_cn: 本研究提出FinCAD方法，通过上下文感知解码的推理时适应技术，减轻大型语言模型（LLM）在金融回溯测试中的参数前瞻性偏差。该方法通过对抗性偏差发现流程和实体-日期自适应规则，显著降低了模型对历史数据的记忆影响，提高了回溯测试的可靠性。在五大市值股票和多个LLM模型的测试中，FinCAD显著改善了样本内外表现的相关性，为基于LLM的交易策略提供了更准确的评估框架。

title: From Uncertainty to Failure Attribution: Self-Diagnosing Models for Failure Attribution under Distribution Shift
summary: Distribution shift poses a significant challenge to the robustness of machine learning models, but the current solutions only aim to detect out-of-distribution (OOD) samples and predict uncertainty levels. We introduce a problem setting for failure attribution under distribution shift, which enables the models not only to detect OOD samples, but also to find out the reason for their failure. The solution we propose is called self-diagnosing models, which are capable of jointly learning predictive output, predictive uncertainty, and a failure attribution signal. In particular, we use the failure attribution vector, produced by a neural network, which provides a structured representation of predictive unreliability by distinguishing four different types of failures: covariance shift, semantic shift, noise corruption, and adversarial perturbation. In other words, we move from scalar uncertainty towards failure identification. For training the model, we introduce a consistency regularizer that encourages consistency between uncertainty and failure attribution predictions. Moreover, to be able to evaluate the model on its ability to find the reasons for failure, we construct several distribution shift benchmarks with predefined mechanisms for generating distribution shifts.
core_methodology: The paper introduces self-diagnosing models that jointly learn predictive output, uncertainty, and failure attribution signals under distribution shift. The models use a failure attribution vector to distinguish between different types of failures such as covariance shift, semantic shift, noise corruption, and adversarial perturbation. A consistency regularizer is used to ensure alignment between uncertainty and failure attribution predictions.
data_sources: The paper constructs several distribution shift benchmarks with predefined mechanisms for generating distribution shifts, but specific financial data sources are not mentioned. However, the methodology can be adapted to financial time series or alternative data.
alpha_potential: The ability to diagnose and attribute failures under distribution shift can enhance the robustness of trading models, particularly in volatile or regime-changing markets. This can help in dynamically adjusting strategies or risk parameters when the model detects specific types of distribution shifts, potentially reducing drawdowns and improving risk-adjusted returns.
title_cn: 从不确定性到失败归因：分布偏移下的自诊断模型
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种自诊断模型，能够在分布偏移下不仅检测异常样本，还能识别失败原因。这一方法可应用于量化交易中，通过识别协变量偏移、语义偏移等失败类型，动态调整策略，提升模型在市场环境变化中的稳健性和适应性。

title: Soft Fitted Q-Iteration without Bellman Completeness: Occupancy Reweighting and Temperature Annealing
summary: Fitted \(Q\)-iteration (FQI) is a standard regression-based method for optimal control in offline reinforcement learning, but its stability under function approximation often relies on Bellman completeness, which requires Bellman images of the fitted class to remain in the class. We study Kullback--Leibler (KL)-regularized, or soft, FQI relative to a fixed reference policy without this assumption. Our key insight is that soft control locally inherits the contraction of policy evaluation in a discounted-occupancy norm. At the soft-optimal fixed point, the linearization of the soft Bellman operator is exactly the Bellman operator for the soft-optimal policy, which contracts in its discounted-occupancy norm; projection in the same norm preserves this contraction. Standard soft FQI instead projects under the offline state-action distribution and need not preserve this property. Motivated by this observation, we propose \emph{occupancy-reweighted soft FQI}, which retains standard Bellman targets and least-squares updates while reweighting regressions by discounted-occupancy ratios induced by the current soft policy. Under \(Q\)-function realizability and local regularity, we establish local contraction and finite-sample convergence with estimated ratios, without Bellman completeness. We then use temperature annealing to convert the local result into global convergence from arbitrary initialization: sufficiently high temperature provides a globally contractive starting regime, while gradual cooling connects successive local contraction regions to any prescribed positive target temperature. Under an action-gap margin condition, switching at a fixed positive temperature to hard FQI with refreshed occupancy weights also yields population and finite-sample convergence to the unregularized optimum.
core_methodology: Soft Fitted Q-Iteration (FQI) with KL regularization, without relying on Bellman completeness. The method includes occupancy reweighting and temperature annealing to ensure convergence under Q-function realizability and local regularity.
data_sources: The abstract does not specify data sources, but the methodology is applicable to any offline reinforcement learning setting, which in finance could include historical market data, order book data, or other financial time series.
alpha_potential: The method's ability to handle offline reinforcement learning without Bellman completeness could improve the stability and convergence of Q-learning-based trading strategies. The occupancy reweighting and temperature annealing techniques may help in adapting to changing market conditions and improving policy optimization.
title_cn: 无需贝尔曼完备性的软拟合Q迭代：占用重加权与温度退火
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种无需贝尔曼完备性的软拟合Q迭代方法，通过占用重加权和温度退火技术，提高了离线强化学习中的策略优化稳定性。该方法适用于金融市场中的历史数据学习，有望提升交易策略的收敛性和适应性。

title: Prediction-Powered Conditional Inference
summary: We study prediction-powered conditional inference in the setting where labeled data are scarce, unlabeled covariates are abundant, and a black-box machine-learning predictor is available. The goal is to perform statistical inference on conditional functionals evaluated at a fixed target point, such as conditional means, without imposing a parametric model for the conditional relationship. Our approach combines localization with prediction-based variance reduction. First, we introduce an RKHS localization method that learns a data-adaptive weight from covariates and reformulates the target conditional moment at the target point as a weighted unconditional moment. Second, we incorporate machine-learning predictions through a correction-based decomposition of this localized moment, yielding a prediction-powered estimator and confidence interval that reduce variance when the predictor is informative while preserving validity regardless of predictor accuracy. We establish nonasymptotic error bounds and, in the abundant-unlabeled regime, minimax-optimal convergence rates for the resulting estimator, prove pointwise asymptotic normality with consistent variance estimation, and provide an explicit variance decomposition that characterizes how machine-learning predictions and unlabeled covariates improve statistical efficiency. Numerical experiments on simulated and real datasets demonstrate valid conditional coverage and substantially sharper confidence intervals than alternative methods.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a method for prediction-powered conditional inference using RKHS localization and a correction-based decomposition of localized moments. It combines machine-learning predictions with statistical inference to estimate conditional functionals like conditional means without imposing parametric models.
data_sources: The method can be applied to any dataset with scarce labeled data and abundant unlabeled covariates. In trading, this could include market data (e.g., price, volume) and alternative data (e.g., news sentiment, macroeconomic indicators).
alpha_potential: The methodology could be used to enhance trading signals by improving the estimation of conditional moments (e.g., expected returns or volatility) at specific target points, leveraging both labeled and unlabeled data. This could lead to more accurate models for momentum strategies, factor investing, or portfolio optimization.
title_cn: 预测驱动的条件推断
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种结合机器学习和统计推断的方法，用于在标记数据稀缺、未标记协变量丰富的情况下进行条件推断。在量化交易中，该方法可用于改进条件矩（如预期收益或波动率）的估计，从而增强交易信号，适用于动量策略、因子投资和组合优化等场景。

title: The Convergence Rate of Stochastic Tracking with Application to Optimal Execution
summary: We study the quadratic tracking problem of a general stochastic target process with absolutely continuous controls, with and without terminal constraint. We derive explicit, non-asymptotic upper bounds in terms of a Besov-type modulus of the target. These bounds yield sharp explicit rates that specialize to the square-root order for semimartingale targets. We then apply these results to a generalized Obizhaeva--Wang execution model with random terminal inventory. We first develop a Hilbert-space approach to characterize its optimal strategy, which includes jumps. To avoid such trading spikes, one regularizes the problem by a quadratic trading-rate penalty with coefficient $\varepsilon$. We then show that the regularized optimal execution cost---and therefore the excess price impact cost of the regularized optimal strategy---converges at the sharp rate $O(\sqrt{\varepsilon})$. Since the regularized optimal strategy is not available in closed form, we further construct a nearly optimal strategy which is readily implementable and shares the same approximation rate.
core_methodology: The paper presents a stochastic tracking problem with absolutely continuous controls, deriving explicit non-asymptotic upper bounds and sharp rates for target processes. It applies these results to optimal execution models, introducing both a rigorous Hilbert-space approach for optimal strategy characterization and a practical regularization technique to avoid trading jumps.
data_sources: The abstract does not specify particular data sources, but the methodology is applicable to standard market data used in execution models (e.g., order book data, trade data).
alpha_potential: The approach offers potential alpha through improved execution strategies in a generalized Obizhaeva-Wang framework, with explicit convergence rates for regularized solutions. This can reduce market impact costs in portfolio transitions and algorithmic execution.
title_cn: 随机跟踪问题的收敛速率及其在最优执行中的应用
summary_cn: 本文研究了具有绝对连续控制的随机跟踪问题，获得了非渐近上界和最优收敛速率。该理论被应用于广义Obizhaeva-Wang最优执行模型，通过二次交易率惩罚的调节方法，证明了正则化后的最优执行成本以√ε速率收敛。研究提供了既避免交易跳跃又保持近似最优性能的实用策略，对算法交易中的执行成本优化具有直接应用价值。

title: Optimal Block Time for AMM Liquidity Providers under Jump-Diffusion Prices
summary: Loss-versus-Rebalancing (LVR) is the dominant adverse-selection cost borne by liquidity providers on automated market makers. Under geometric Brownian motion, arbitrage profit scales with the probability of a profitable block, which vanishes as the block time $\Delta t \to 0$; this is the standing argument for ever-shorter blocks. Modeling the reference price instead as a jump-diffusion, I show that the constant-product LVR rate splits into a diffusion channel carrying the known multiplier $F(\gamma/(\sigma\sqrt{\Delta t}))$ and a jump channel $\lambda V \cdot G(\gamma;m,\delta^2)$ carrying no $\Delta t$, the two interacting only through an explicitly bounded remainder. The block schedule therefore governs only one channel. For symmetric jump laws the jump channel is moreover an exact lower bound, $\ell(\Delta t) \ge \lambda V G > 0$, so the rate does not vanish as $\Delta t \to 0$, and descends slowly, as $\sqrt{\Delta t}$. At Ethereum's calibrated 12-second slot the rate is 471 bp/yr against a floor of 125, so only three quarters of LP loss is schedule-addressable. At Solana's 400 ms slot the jump channel already dominates. Netting the rate against per-block consensus cost, the LP-side optimal block time is invariant in pool size and in every jump parameter $(\lambda,m,\delta)$: jumps shift the level of LP loss but not the planner's marginal tradeoff. Volatility, the fee tier, and consensus cost set the optimum, near 8 s. However, LVR is only one input to block-time welfare, so this bounds the LP-side contribution rather than settling the design question.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a jump-diffusion model for evaluating the optimal block time for liquidity providers on automated market makers, incorporating both diffusion and jump channels. The methodology includes mathematical derivations to split the LVR rate into these channels and calculates their respective contributions.
data_sources: The analysis is based on blockchain data, specifically referencing Ethereum and Solana for empirical validation. The paper uses calibrated parameters for these blockchains to estimate LVR rates.
alpha_potential: By understanding and modeling the split between diffusion and jump channels, the paper provides insights into how liquidity providers can better protect themselves from adverse selection (LVR). This could help in designing more efficient trading strategies and selecting optimal block times, thereby reducing losses for liquidity providers and enhancing market efficiency.
title_cn: 基于跳跃-扩散价格模型的AMM流动性提供者最优区块时间研究
summary_cn: 该论文研究自动做市商(AMM)中流动性提供者的最优区块时间,利用跳跃-扩散价格模型分析资产价格动态。研究发现LVR损失率在连续交易下不趋近于零,并提出区块时间仅影响扩散通道而非跳跃通道。通过以太坊和Solana的实证数据验证了理论模型,推导出流动性提供者的最优区块时间约为8秒。这为加密市场做市策略和区块时间设计提供了重要参考。

title: Metaorder modelling and identification from public data
summary: Market-order flow in financial markets exhibits long-range correlations. This is a widely known stylised fact of financial markets. A popular hypothesis for this stylised fact comes from the Lillo-Mike-Farmer (LMF) order-splitting theory. However, quantitative tests of this theory have historically relied on proprietary datasets with trader identifiers, limiting reproducibility and cross-market validation. We investigate whether it can be recovered from anonymous public data using synthetic metaorder reconstruction. Using transaction and quote data for the largest 239 stocks by market capitalisation on the JSE as of 13 March 2026 with the data range being 1 January 2023 until 31 December 2025, we conduct a grid search over reconstruction parameters and evaluate each configuration against established metaorder stylised facts and the LMF relation. Configurations selected to minimise errors across the metaorder impact stylised facts reproduce the targeted aggregate properties but yield a poor LMF relation. Configurations selected to minimise the LMF discrepancy recover the relation by construction while retaining several broad impact features, although some stock-level execution and decay fits are weaker. These asymmetric results show that recovering aggregate impact stylised facts alone is insufficient to identify LMF-consistent order splitting, while the LMF-targeted result establishes compatibility within the reconstruction class rather than an independent test. The findings support consistency with, rather than direct validation of, the LMF theory using anonymous market data.
core_methodology: The paper employs synthetic metaorder reconstruction from public market data to test the Lillo-Mike-Farmer (LMF) order-splitting theory, using a grid search over reconstruction parameters to evaluate against established metaorder stylised facts and the LMF relation.
data_sources: Transaction and quote data for the largest 239 stocks by market capitalisation on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) from 1 January 2023 until 31 December 2025.
alpha_potential: The methodology could provide insights into detecting hidden metaorders in public data, which is valuable for predicting short-term price movements and optimizing execution strategies. However, the asymmetric results suggest that while aggregate impact stylised facts can be recovered, direct validation of LMF theory is more challenging.
title_cn: 基于公开数据的元订单建模与识别
summary_cn: 本研究通过公开市场数据合成元订单重建，测试Lillo-Mike-Farmer (LMF)订单分割理论。虽然研究支持LMF理论的兼容性，但需注意其直接验证仍存在局限。该方法有助于从公开数据中发现隐藏元订单，对短期价格预测和交易执行优化具有潜在应用价值。

title: The Value of Information: A Puzzle
summary: We show that the total value of information to informed traders can be measured by the covariation between price changes and order flow. This covariation captures noise trader losses, which equal informed trader gains when market making is competitive. We estimate the value of information using high frequency data on US equities at $3.5 million per year. The aggregate value of information is 0.04% of market cap, considerably lower than the 0.67% in fees investors pay searching for superior returns according to French (2008), which we extend through 2024. We discuss potential resolutions for these puzzling findings.
core_methodology: The paper measures the value of information to informed traders by analyzing the covariation between price changes and order flow, capturing noise trader losses which equal informed trader gains under competitive market making conditions. This approach provides a direct quantification of information asymmetry in markets.
data_sources: High frequency data on US equities is used to estimate the value of information, showing real-world applicability and relevance to equity markets.
alpha_potential: The methodology identifies the extent to which informed traders profit from information asymmetry, suggesting potential strategies to either capture similar information edges or to develop models that can predict or exploit periods of heightened information asymmetry.
title_cn: 信息的价值：一个谜题
summary_cn: 本文通过分析价格变化与订单流的协变关系，量化了信息对知情交易者的价值，揭示了竞争性做市条件下噪声交易者的损失等于知情交易者的收益。利用美国股票的高频数据估算，年信息总价值达350万美元，占市值的0.04%，显著低于投资者为寻求超额回报支付的费用（0.67%）。研究结果为开发基于信息不对称的交易策略提供了理论基础。

title: AlgoWorlds: Benchmarking Tool Use for Global Optimization in Algorithmic Worlds
summary: Tool-use benchmarks generally evaluate whether an agent completes a workflow using appropriate tools and valid arguments. However, feasibility alone is insufficient in real-world decision settings such as route planning and fleet dispatch. Individual choices interact through shared constraints and costs, so a feasible solution may still be substantially suboptimal. This raises a harder question: can an agent turn information gathered through tools into a globally optimal decision? We introduce AlgoWorlds, a benchmark that transforms formally specified combinatorial optimization problems into partially observed decision environments with verifiable global optima. Each environment contains a hidden instance observed only through task-specific information tools, after which the agent commits to one structured decision evaluated for feasibility and optimality. AlgoWorlds contains 240 environments covering ten combinatorial optimization families and four workload levels. Family-specific deterministic programs generate the instances, exact algorithms certify their optima and determine workload levels, and two structurally different tool interfaces present each underlying instance. We evaluate seven leading LLMs, including Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.6 Sol. Achieving global optimality remains highly challenging: although leading models produce feasible decisions in most cases, the best-performing model reaches exact optimality in only 38.61% of cases. Even when agents collect sufficient information to reconstruct the hidden instance, most failures end in feasible but suboptimal decisions. The challenge therefore extends beyond information acquisition to information integration, global constraint reasoning, and decision verification. The project homepage is available at https://xzx34.github.io/AlgoWorlds/, and the code is available at https://github.com/xzx34/AlgoWorlds.
core_methodology: The paper introduces AlgoWorlds, a benchmark that transforms combinatorial optimization problems into partially observed decision environments with verifiable global optima. It evaluates how agents (LLMs) can use task-specific information tools to make globally optimal decisions.
data_sources: Synthetic data generated from deterministic programs for combinatorial optimization problems across ten families and four workload levels.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted for portfolio optimization and trade execution strategies where global optimization is crucial. The challenges identified (information integration, global constraint reasoning) are directly relevant to algorithmic trading systems.
title_cn: 算法世界：用于全局优化的工具使用基准测试
summary_cn: 该研究提出了AlgoWorlds基准，评估智能体在部分可观察环境中通过工具使用实现全局优化的能力。对于量化交易，其方法可应用于投资组合优化和交易执行策略的全局决策，特别解决了信息整合和全局约束推理等关键挑战。

title: Denoising as Projection: Constrained Optimization with Gradient-Guided Diffusion
summary: Diffusion models are increasingly used not only for sampling from learned data distributions, but also for generating samples that optimize task-specific objectives. A common approach is to guide the reverse diffusion process using gradients of an external objective. However, when the data distribution is supported on a structured feasible set, such as a manifold or a constraint set, gradient guidance can move samples away from the learned data geometry. In this paper, we study a simple projected-gradient-guided diffusion update based on the observation that the Stein denoising operator can act as an approximate projection onto the data geometry. The proposed update incorporates the objective gradient inside the denoising step, yielding an inference-time method that uses only a pretrained denoiser and gradient evaluations. We analyze this update as an inexact projected-gradient method for constrained optimization over learned feasible geometries. Our theory covers three settings: linear manifolds, compact convex feasible sets, and compact Riemannian submanifolds. In all these settings, we prove descent and finite-time convergence guarantees. Numerical experiments support the theoretical interpretation and illustrate how the proposed update balances objective descent with preservation of the learned geometry.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a constrained optimization method using gradient-guided diffusion with a denoising step that acts as an approximate projection onto the data geometry. This approach balances objective optimization with preservation of the learned data structure.
data_sources: The paper does not specify particular financial datasets but implies applicability to any structured data representing financial time series or market states.
alpha_potential: The method could be adapted to optimize trading signals or portfolio weights under structural constraints, potentially improving signal-to-noise ratios in noisy financial data.
title_cn: 去噪即投影：基于梯度引导扩散的约束优化
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种结合梯度引导扩散与去噪操作的约束优化方法，在保持数据结构的同时优化目标函数。在量化交易中，这种方法可应用于噪声市场数据的信号优化或带约束的资产配置问题，通过结构感知的优化提升策略鲁棒性。

title: LoGo: Token-Level Dynamic Local-Global Attention
summary: As context lengths scale, attention increasingly becomes a primary computational bottleneck in large language models. Standard Transformers remain powerful but computationally inefficient, as they allocate the same attention budget to every token regardless of its contextual demand. Existing local-global hybrids provide a more efficient alternative by mixing restricted- and full-context attention, but they typically allocate span statically across layers or heads. To address these limitations, we propose LoGo, a token-level dynamic local-global attention mechanism that uses attention span as a direct proxy for attention budget allocation. Each LoGo layer contains coupled local and global branches: all tokens receive efficient local attention over a restricted context window, while a learned gate activates global attention with full-context access only for tokens requiring long-range information. A threshold-based budget controller maintains a target global ratio without auxiliary losses, and a progressive masking schedule stabilizes training before sparse routing takes effect. We further implement query-sparse Triton kernels that convert reduced global-attention computation into practical speedups. Extensive experiments validate LoGo's effectiveness, showing that it preserves the scaling behavior of full-attention Transformers across model sizes. In controlled comparisons, LoGo improves over the full-attention Transformer and matched-budget static local-global hybrids, with clear gains on long-range retrieval. Analysis further shows that LoGo learns interpretable span allocation patterns. These results suggest that learned token-level span allocation is an effective and scalable way to improve the long-context performance-compute trade-off.
core_methodology: Token-level dynamic local-global attention mechanism that allocates attention span based on contextual demand, using coupled local and global branches with learned gating for global attention activation.
data_sources: Likely text or sequence data (e.g., financial reports, news, earnings calls), though not explicitly stated in the abstract.
alpha_potential: Potential to improve processing of long-context financial data (e.g., earnings transcripts, regulatory filings) by efficiently capturing long-range dependencies while maintaining computational efficiency.
title_cn: LoGo：基于令牌级别的动态局部-全局注意力机制
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种动态局部-全局注意力机制（LoGo），可优化长上下文数据处理效率。对量化交易的潜在价值在于：1）高效处理长文本金融数据（如财报、新闻）；2）通过自适应注意力分配捕捉关键远距信息；3）计算高效性适合实时应用。适用于事件驱动型策略和基本面分析自动化。

title: Adaptive Doubly Robust Off-Policy Evaluation for Ranking Policies under Diverse User Behavior
summary: Off-policy evaluation (OPE) of ranking policies is challenging be- cause selecting and ordering multiple items from a candidate set makes the number of possible rankings grow combinatorially with the number of candidates and the ranking length. Consequently, Inverse Propensity Scoring (IPS), whose importance weight is the full-ranking probability ratio under the evaluation and logging policies, can have excessive variance. Independent IPS (IIPS) and Reward Interaction IPS (RIPS) reduce variance by imposing fixed assumptions on how users browse rankings, but may introduce bias when those assumptions mismatch actual behavior. Adaptive Inverse Propensity Scoring (AIPS) addresses this trade-off by adap- tively marginalizing importance weights over the actions that affect each position-wise reward. It attains minimum variance within a class of unbiased IPS-based estimators when the true user be- havior model is observed. However, its estimation accuracy may still degrade for longer rankings, and AIPS does not use a reward model for residual correction. We propose Adaptive Doubly Robust (ADR), which combines adaptive importance weighting with re- ward regression through a control-variate correction. We establish its unbiasedness when the true user behavior model is observed and characterize a sufficient condition under which it reduces vari- ance relative to AIPS. Across synthetic experiments with 10,000 simulations per condition, ADR improves mean squared error over AIPS and conventional ranking OPE estimators across a range of logged-data sizes and ranking lengths.
core_methodology: Adaptive Doubly Robust (ADR) method for off-policy evaluation in ranking policies, combining adaptive importance weighting with reward regression through control-variate correction.
data_sources: Synthetic data from simulations; potentially applicable to user interaction data in trading platforms or ranking financial products.
alpha_potential: Potential application in optimizing ranking of financial products or trading signals based on user behavior, though requires adaptation to financial contexts.
title_cn: 针对多样化用户行为下排名策略的自适应双重鲁棒离策略评估
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种自适应双重鲁棒方法(ADR)，用于在用户行为多样化的背景下评估排名策略的离策略效果。该方法通过结合自适应重要性加权与奖励回归的控制变量校正，减少了估计方差，适用于金融产品的排名优化或交易信号的排序策略评估。

title: AgenticRag-R1: Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Stack Memory for Multi-Step Reasoning, Retrieval and Memorizing
summary: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) improves the factuality of large language models (LLMs), yet existing RAG systems often struggle with complex, multi-step reasoning that requires adaptive retrieval and continuous revision of intermediate contexts. Recent reinforcement learning (RL)-based agentic RAG methods partially alleviate this issue, but typically rely on coarse-grained action spaces and trajectory-level rewards, resulting in weak reward assignment and a bias toward short-horizon, stereotyped reasoning template. To address, we propose AgenticRag-R1, a RL framework that deeply integrates reasoning, retrieval, and memory via a memory stack and fine-grained action space, supported by hierarchical action-aware rewards and an information-aware trajectory rejection strategy to enable effective long-horizon learning. Experiments across a diverse set of multi-hop, open-domain, and agentic reasoning benchmarks, spanning multiple backbone model sizes, demonstrate that AgenticRag-R1 consistently outperforms strong baselines. Moreover, AgenticRag-R1 learns more robust, interpretable, and memory-aware reasoning behaviors, highlighting the effect of fine-grained action modeling and information-aware optimization for long-horizon reasoning. Our code is anonymous available at https://github.com/jiangxinke/Harness-RL/tree/AgenticRAG-R1-Whitebox.
core_methodology: Reinforcement Learning framework integrating reasoning, retrieval, and memory via a memory stack and fine-grained action space, with hierarchical action-aware rewards and an information-aware trajectory rejection strategy for long-horizon learning.
data_sources: Not explicitly financial data, but method is tested on multi-hop, open-domain, and agentic reasoning benchmarks implying potential adaptation for market data analysis.
alpha_potential: Potential to enhance multi-step reasoning in algorithmic trading strategies that require adaptive use of complex, evolving market information, though direct financial application would require significant domain-specific adaptation.
title_cn: AgenticRag-R1：基于栈式记忆的多步推理、检索与记忆的代理强化学习框架
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一个强化学习框架，通过细粒度动作空间和记忆栈技术改进多步推理能力。虽然未直接测试金融场景，但其自适应检索和分层奖励机制可能优化需要复杂市场分析的交易策略（如事件套利、多因子组合管理）。技术亮点包括信息感知的轨迹拒绝策略和可解释的推理行为学习，适用于需要长期序列决策的交易场景。

title: LLMODE: Aligning ODEs with LLMs via Gated Token Injection for Irregular Spatio-Temporal Forecasting
summary: Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise for spatio-temporal forecasting, but existing approaches often rely on regularly sampled token sequences and struggle with irregular observations because of temporal asynchrony, representation-space misalignment, and limited context windows. We propose LLMODE, a token-efficient framework for irregular spatio-temporal forecasting with a frozen LLM backbone. LLMODE first uses a graph-aware ODE encoder to reconstruct irregular graph observations as a continuous-time latent trajectory. A Fixed-Budget Perceiver Resampler then compresses this variable-length trajectory into a fixed number of dynamic memory tokens. In parallel, compact statistical descriptors are encoded and resampled into context memory tokens. A dual-source gated cross-attention module injects both memories into the frozen LLM, enabling controlled utilization of external spatio-temporal evidence. Experiments on three real-world urban datasets and two physical-dynamics benchmarks show competitive overall performance, with clearer advantages under sparse or dynamically complex irregular sampling. Additional evaluations on unseen urban regions further demonstrate strong zero-shot generalization without adaptation.
core_methodology: LLMODE integrates a graph-aware ODE encoder with a frozen LLM backbone to handle irregular spatio-temporal data, using gated token injection for improved forecasting.
data_sources: Real-world urban datasets and physical-dynamics benchmarks, implying potential adaptation to market or alternative financial data with irregular sampling.
alpha_potential: The framework's ability to handle irregular and sparse data could be leveraged for predicting market movements or sentiment analysis from non-uniform financial data streams.
title_cn: LLMODE：通过门控令牌注入将ODE与LLM对齐以实现不规则时空预测
summary_cn: LLMODE提出了一种结合ODE和LLM的方法，用于处理不规则时空数据，通过门控令牌注入提升预测精度。在金融领域，该方法可能适用于处理非均匀采样的市场数据或情感分析，为量化交易提供新的信号源。

title: Reward-guided Fine-Tuning of One-Step Generative Models via Wasserstein Gradient Flow
summary: To mitigate the time complexity of generative models, one-step generative models have recently emerged through direct mapping from noise to data in a single forward pass. However, the reward-guided fine-tuning method of one-step generative models remains largely unexplored. To address this, we consider one-step generators from an optimal transport view, investigating Wasserstein Gradient Flow (WGF) for modeling smooth and controlled distributional evolution in probability space. We then propose a novel reward-guided fine-tuning of a one-step generative model via WGF. We derive a practical training method that requires no reward gradients, thereby handling both non-differentiable and differentiable rewards. Moreover, our method provides smooth and stable reward-guided distributional updates while mitigating reward hacking and mode collapse. Experiments on 2D synthetic data, CIFAR-10, and ImageNet 256$\times$256 with diverse rewards, including JPEG (in)compressibility, class probability, Black-and-White and CLIP alignment, show that our method achieves better reward alignment compared to baselines.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a reward-guided fine-tuning method for one-step generative models using Wasserstein Gradient Flow (WGF). This approach allows for smooth and controlled distributional evolution in probability space, applicable to both non-differentiable and differentiable rewards.
data_sources: The paper uses synthetic 2D data, CIFAR-10, and ImageNet 256×256 with diverse rewards including JPEG (in)compressibility, class probability, Black-and-White, and CLIP alignment. While not directly financial, the methodology could be adapted to market or alternative financial data.
alpha_potential: The method could potentially be used to generate synthetic financial data or optimize trading signals by aligning with specific reward functions, such as risk-adjusted returns or arbitrage opportunities. However, this would require substantial adaptation and validation in financial contexts.

title: ECA-BLS: An Efficient Complex-Augmented Broad Learning System
summary: Broad Learning System (BLS) is an efficient alternative to deep architectures due to its fast training, analytical learning, and strong generalization under limited data. However, existing BLS variants are confined to real-valued representations, restricting their ability to capture nonlinear interactions and second-order statistical dependencies inherent in real-world data. Notably, no prior BLS model fully exploits the complete second-order statistics that naturally emerge when data are embedded in the complex domain. To address this limitation, this paper introduces the first complex augmented Broad Learning System (CA-BLS), which transforms real-valued inputs into phase-encoded complex representations and adopts widely linear modeling to jointly leverage covariance and pseudo-covariance information via complex conjugate augmentation. This enables effective modeling of latent nonlinearities, coherence structures, and second-order dependencies inaccessible to conventional BLS formulations. To mitigate the additional computational cost of complex augmentation, an Efficient Complex Augmented BLS (ECA-BLS) is further developed, reformulating CA-BLS entirely in the real domain while preserving its exact decision function, achieving up to 75\% fewer multiplications and over 60\% fewer additions. A rigorous theoretical analysis proves the mathematical equivalence between CA-BLS and ECA-BLS, ensuring zero theoretical loss. Extensive experiments on 26 benchmark datasets from the UCI and KEEL repositories demonstrate that ECA-BLS consistently outperforms classical BLS and recent state-of-the-art randomized neural networks in accuracy, average rank, and statistical significance, establishing augmented second-order modeling as a critical and previously missing dimension of BLS research.
core_methodology: The paper introduces an Efficient Complex Augmented Broad Learning System (ECA-BLS), which transforms real-valued inputs into phase-encoded complex representations to capture second-order statistical dependencies. It uses widely linear modeling to leverage covariance and pseudo-covariance information via complex conjugate augmentation, enhancing the modeling of nonlinear interactions and coherence structures.
data_sources: The paper evaluates the methodology on 26 benchmark datasets from the UCI and KEEL repositories, which are general-purpose datasets not specifically related to financial markets.
alpha_potential: The ECA-BLS methodology could potentially be adapted to financial time series data to capture complex nonlinear dependencies and second-order statistics, which are often present in market data. This could lead to improved prediction models for asset prices or volatility, but the paper does not demonstrate this directly.
title_cn: ECA-BLS：一种高效的复数增强型广度学习系统
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种高效的复数增强型广度学习系统（ECA-BLS），通过将实值输入转换为相位编码的复数表示，利用广泛的线性建模联合协方差和伪协方差信息，捕捉非线性交互和二级统计依赖。在通用基准数据集上表现优异，虽未直接应用于金融数据，但其方法可能提升金融时间序列预测模型的表现。

title: Uncertainty-Driven Replay Memory for Reinforcement Learning
summary: Uncertainty estimation provides promising capabilities for reinforcement learning (RL) agents. Notably, estimating uncertainty can reduce the training time and enable agents to obtain greater rewards over time by exploiting information related to whether an action would facilitate exploration of portions of an environment that are well-known versus those that are relatively unknown. In this work, we propose a novel formulation of the experience replay buffer commonly used in RL that we call uncertainty-driven replay memory (UDRM), which entails an update scheme for internally stored memories based on uncertainty estimates obtained by an RL model during training. In contrast to existing forms of RL, which typically use temporal difference error or the distribution of transitions to update the replay memory buffer and train RL controllers, our scheme biases the memory buffer to store more uncertain transitions that will improve an RL agent's generalization throughout training. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed uncertainty-aware replay buffer enables an RL agent to obtain higher rewards during training compared to other existing uncertainty-aware RL frameworks.
core_methodology: Proposes an uncertainty-driven replay memory (UDRM) for reinforcement learning, which biases the memory buffer to store more uncertain transitions to improve an RL agent's generalization during training.
data_sources: Not specified in the abstract, but typically RL in finance would use market data such as price, volume, and order book data.
alpha_potential: Potential to improve RL-based trading strategies by focusing on uncertain market conditions, which could lead to better exploration and exploitation of market inefficiencies.
title_cn: 不确定性驱动的强化学习回放记忆
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种不确定性驱动的回放记忆方法（UDRM），通过偏好存储高不确定性的状态转换，提升强化学习代理在训练中的泛化能力。在量化交易中，该方法可能帮助交易算法更好地探索未知市场状态，从而发现潜在的市场无效性。虽然未明确使用金融数据，但其方法论可迁移至基于强化学习的交易策略开发。

title: Partially Linear Autoencoders for Manifold Learning and Dimensionality Reduction
summary: Autoencoders are widely used for nonlinear dimensionality reduction and manifold learning. While most common implementations rely on both nonlinear encoders and decoders, we investigate the specific role of the encoder and the extent to which it can be constrained to be linear without reducing accuracy. We conduct a comparative study on four autoencoder architectures: standard fully nonlinear autoencoders (AE), linear-encoder autoencoders (Lenc-AE), linear-decoder autoencoders (Ldec-AE), and fully linear autoencoders (LAE), evaluated on synthetic manifolds, computational mechanics data sets, and real-world image data sets including MNIST. We demonstrate that imposing a linear encoder preserves most of the representational capacity of the autoencoder, provided the decoder remains nonlinear. In particular, Lenc-AE consistently outperforms both Ldec-AE and LAE, and achieves reconstruction quality comparable to fully nonlinear AE, while offering advantages in terms of parsimony and interpretability of the latent representation. These results suggest that the nonlinear decoder is the critical component for manifold learning, rather than the encoder. A geometric interpretation of this finding is developed, which identifies the precise conditions under which a linear encoder is sufficient, and the specific manifold configurations that expose its limitations.
core_methodology: The paper investigates partially linear autoencoders, specifically comparing architectures where either the encoder or decoder is constrained to be linear while the other remains nonlinear. The focus is on understanding the role of nonlinearity in manifold learning and dimensionality reduction, with findings that a nonlinear decoder is more critical than a nonlinear encoder for preserving representational capacity.
data_sources: The study uses synthetic manifolds, computational mechanics data sets, and real-world image data sets including MNIST. While not directly financial data, the methodologies could be adapted to market data or alternative data like order book dynamics or high-frequency price series.
alpha_potential: The approach could be valuable for feature extraction and dimensionality reduction in quantitative finance, particularly for nonlinear relationships in market data. The linear encoder's interpretability might help in identifying factor exposures or latent market states, while the nonlinear decoder captures complex relationships without overfitting.
title_cn: 用于流形学习和降维的部分线性自编码器
summary_cn: 该研究探讨线性编码器与非线性和解码器的自编码架构，证明非线性解码器对保持表征能力更为关键，而线性编码器仍可保持良好性能。这一发现可应用于金融市场数据降维和特征提取，尤其适合捕捉市场中的非线性关系，同时提供更易解释的潜在表示。

title: SearchWiki: Learning to Build and Navigate Knowledge Wikis for Active Information Seeking
summary: Flat retrieval-augmented generation treats a corpus as a bag of chunks, discarding document hierarchy and cross document structure. We introduce SearchWiki, a harness framework that synthesizes a corpus into a hierarchical, typed, navigable wiki and trains an agent, WikiResearcher-9B, to retrieve information through multi-turn tool use. The wiki organizes knowledge into three layers - document overviews, cross- document topic pages, and page-level source records; enabling progressive refinement of retrieval when initial lookup misses. We optimize the agent's navigation policy with on-policy reinforcement learning with a multi-component reward function balancing answer correctness, retrieval quality and trajectory efficiency. Evaluation on ViDoRe-V3 (8 domains), FinanceBench, and memory benchmarks (LoCoMo, LongMemEval, PersonaMem-v2) shows that WikiResearcher- 9B which is our RL-tuned Qwen 9B model, significantly outperforms same-size untrained baselines and exceeds or matches larger external models. SearchWiki paired with WikiResearcher-9B demonstrates that learned navigation over structured corpora is a superior alternative to flat retrieval.
core_methodology: Hierarchical knowledge organization and reinforcement learning-based navigation for information retrieval
data_sources: Financial benchmarks (FinanceBench) and other domain-specific datasets
alpha_potential: Potential to improve research efficiency and information retrieval accuracy for quantitative finance professionals, though not directly generating alpha signals
title_cn: SearchWiki：学习构建和导航知识维基以实现主动信息搜索
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种分层知识组织和强化学习导航的系统，可提升金融领域信息检索效率和准确性。虽然不直接产生交易信号，但对量化研究员的信息处理能力有显著提升价值。
